title: Wersestadion - Grokipedia
content: The **Wersestadion** is a multi-use stadium located in Ahlen, Germany, primarily used for football matches and serving as the home ground for the fifth-tier club Rot Weiss Ahlen.](#ref-1) With a total capacity of 12,500 spectators—including 4,000 covered seats and 8,500 standing places (6,000 of which are covered)—it features a natural grass pitch equipped with undersoil heating and no running track.](#ref-1) Originally established in the 1940s as the Glückaufkampfbahn on its current site along the Werse River, the venue was redeveloped and renamed Wersestadion in 1997, with the stadium structure built that year under the ownership of Rot Weiss Ahlen.](#ref-2)](#ref-1) The club itself was founded in 1996 through a merger of TuS Ahlen and Blau-Weiß Ahlen, initially operating as LR Ahlen before adopting its current name by the 2007/08 season.](#ref-3) Throughout its history, Wersestadion has been central to Rot Weiss Ahlen's development of young talent, notably hosting the early careers of players who achieved international prominence.
